statement: What is the domain of the function $h(x) = \sqrt{10 - 2x} + \dfrac{3}{x^2 - 4}$?

choices.misconception: I made sure the expression under the square root was not negative, but I forgot that the denominator $x^2 - 4$ cannot be $0$.
I divided both sides of $-2x \ge -10$ by $-2$ without flipping the inequality sign, so I got $x \ge 5$.
I solved $x^2 - 4 = 0$ and found only $x = 2$, but $x = -2$ also makes the denominator $0$.

hints: Two things can go wrong: a negative number under the square root, and a zero denominator.
Solve $10 - 2x \ge 0$, remembering to flip the sign when dividing by a negative number. Then remove every $x$ that makes $x^2 - 4 = 0$.
$10 - 2x \ge 0$ gives $x \le 5$, and $x^2 - 4 = 0$ at $x = 2$ and $x = -2$, both of which are less than $5$.

solutions.reliable:
The square root needs $10 - 2x \ge 0$, so $-2x \ge -10$ and, dividing by $-2$ and flipping the sign, $x \le 5$. The fraction needs $x^2 - 4
